hypotheses.statement: EOS suppression is caused primarily by excessive residual magnitude.
hypotheses.evidence: The duration failures are not ordered by the recorded target residual ratios; a scale probe is required.

hypotheses.statement: EOS suppression is caused by insufficient local context.
hypotheses.evidence: target_context_1 rescues Kumar A and reduces Mumbai B relative to target_only, but Kumar B remains long; context alone is insufficient.

hypotheses.statement: The altered pronunciation representation changes early acoustic token choices, which then autoregressively sends Qwen onto a long but internally valid trajectory.
hypotheses.evidence: Case-specific acoustic_eos trajectories and large frame-count changes are consistent with this mechanism; the new per-step trace will test it directly.

hypotheses.statement: There is a runner/decoding inconsistency unrelated to the pronunciation residual.
hypotheses.evidence: The inspected rows use consistent deterministic settings and EOS metadata; no runner-only cause is visible in the artifact.

hypotheses.statement: Termination instability is specific to certain phone-sequence perturbations rather than a general consequence of unseen-name conditioning.
hypotheses.evidence: Kumar B and Mumbai B are unstable while Singh, Mumbai A, Kumar A under target_context_1, and localized controls are short; Dasharatha A/B provides the planned unseen-name test.
